# Requirement Traceability Protocol

## Purpose
Track requirements through the entire development lifecycle:
Requirement → Sub-Task → Code File → Test Case → Review Verdict.

## Trace IDs

**IDs are copied verbatim from whatever produced them. Never renumber, never re-prefix.**
There is no single `REQ-` namespace — the prefix says where the requirement came from, and
that is information worth keeping. A renumbered ID breaks the link back to its source
document, which is the only thing traceability is for.

| Prefix | Assigned by | Source file |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| `UC-{NNN}` | `/bk-spec` Phase 1 — use cases | `bk/dev/{feature}/srs/02-functional-requirements.md` |
| `NFR-{CAT}-{NNN}` | `/bk-spec` Phase 1 — non-functional (CAT: PERF, SEC, …) | `bk/dev/{feature}/srs/03-nonfunctional-requirements.md` |
| `REQ-{NNN}` | `/bk-plan` Step 4b — extracted from enterprise PRD/BRD docs | `{plan-dir}/inputs/requirements.json` |
| `TC-{NNN}` | `/bk-plan` Step 4b — test specs from enterprise docs | `{plan-dir}/inputs/requirements.json` |
| `REQ-{NNN}` | `/bk-plan` Step 3 — derived when no formal source exists | `bk/dev/{feature}/srs.md` |

**Source precedence** when more than one exists for a feature: `/bk-spec` SRS (`UC-`/`NFR-`)
> enterprise docs (`REQ-`/`TC-`) > locally derived (`REQ-`). Requirements from a lower tier
that duplicate a higher one are dropped, not re-ID'd — note the overlap in `plan.md ## Gaps`.

An ID is immutable once written into a sub-task or a matrix.

## Trace Chain

The carrying field is **`reqs:`** in sub-task YAML frontmatter.

Plans written before 0.6.0 spell it `traces:` and often use the old `REQ-{feature}-{NNN}`
IDs. Readers accept `traces:` as an alias and leave those IDs exactly as written — verbatim
applies to legacy IDs too. Nothing writes `traces:` any more; the alias is removed in 0.8.0.

| Stage | File | ID reference |
|-------|------|--------------|
| Requirements | `bk/dev/{feature}/srs/02-*.md`, `srs/03-*.md`, `srs.md`, `inputs/requirements.json` | Defines the IDs |
| Plan | `bk/dev/{feature}/sub-task-NN-*.md` | YAML `reqs: [UC-001, NFR-SEC-001]` |
| Code | Source files | Comment `// @trace {ID}` near implementation |
| Impl report | `research/impl-sub-task-NN.md` | Frontmatter `requirements_satisfied: [...]` |
| Tests | Test files | Test name or comment references the ID |
| Review | Review report | Coverage check against the sub-task's `reqs` |

## Traceability Matrix
Path: `bk/dev/{feature}/traceability-matrix.md`
Generated by bk-project-manager during finalize, by reading each sub-task's `reqs:` field.

Format:
| ID | Description | Sub-Task | Code Files | Tests | Review | Status |
|----|-------------|----------|------------|-------|--------|--------|
| UC-001 | QR scan | sub-task-01 | PaymentVM.swift | testQRScan | Approved | ✅ Covered |
| UC-002 | History | — | — | — | — | ❌ Not implemented |

Coverage = covered / total × 100%. The matrix MUST contain a line matching
`Coverage: {N}%` — `traceability-check.cjs` parses that line and can report nothing without it.

## Integration Points
- **/bk-spec**: assigns `UC-`/`NFR-` IDs when writing the SRS
- **/bk-plan** Step 4b: assigns `REQ-`/`TC-` IDs when extracting enterprise docs
- **/bk-plan** synthesis: writes `reqs:` into each sub-task's YAML frontmatter
- **/bk-code**: dev agents add `// @trace {ID}` comments and list `requirements_satisfied`
  in the impl report
- **bk-project-manager**: generates `traceability-matrix.md` during finalize
- **traceability-check.cjs**: before commit, warns when coverage < 80%, and warns when
  sub-tasks declare `reqs:` but no matrix was generated at all

## Constraints
- IDs are immutable once assigned, and are never renumbered between stages
- Every sub-task SHOULD reference at least 1 ID; a sub-task with `reqs: []` is untraceable
  by construction and must say why in its `## Scope`
- Traceability is recommended for Standard/Complex tiers, optional for Trivial
- A feature whose sub-tasks all carry `reqs:` MUST get a matrix at finalize — silently
  skipping it turns the pre-commit coverage gate into a no-op
